name: Andaz 5th Avenue
positioning: Midtown Manhattan hotel on 5th Avenue, across the street from the main branch of the New York Public Library, with loft-like rooms designed by Tony Chi
best_for: Travelers who want a Midtown base by Bryant Park and the New York Public Library
Guests who like design and art, from loft-like rooms to work by New York City-based artists

facts.text: The hotel is on 5th Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, near the New York Public Library.
The hotel is set across the street from the main branch of the New York Public Library.
Subway lines 7, B, D, F and M can be caught across the street at Bryant Park.
Grand Central Terminal is a 5-minute walk away.
The hotel's building once housed the headquarters of Tommy Hilfiger.
The hotel has a collection of work by New York City-based artists.
The King Bed with City View Deluxe rooms have views of 5th Avenue and the New York Public Library.
Rooms have a minifridge with complimentary snacks and nonalcoholic beverages.
The Bar Downstairs and Kitchen has an open kitchen with bar seating.
In-room dining offers The Bar Downstairs' selection of locally sourced dishes.
The hotel is pet friendly and welcomes dogs.
The hotel has a fitness center.

highlights.text: The guest rooms were designed by Tony Chi and feel like New York City lofts, with 12-foot ceilings and plenty of natural light.
The Empire Terrace Suite has a wraparound terrace with views of the Empire State Building and the New York Public Library.
The hotel has an artists-in-residence program and showcases works by emerging artists in a small gallery space.
The Wellness Suite is a bright corner suite with city views, The Studio Mirror by Lululemon and an oversized soaking tub.
The hotel hosts a complimentary wine hour.

considerations.text: Not all rooms have notable views.
Suite terraces are not furnished during the fall and winter seasons.
Valet parking has no in/out privileges.
